holmes.title: Joshua: The Hebrew and Greek Texts
holmes.author: S. Holmes
holmes.rendering: Ordinary pdftoppm page rendering, longest dimension 2200 pixels except PDF8/23 at2000; no generative processing. Tool display resized the complete pages to1280-pixel width. Render density is not new optical evidence.
controls: Printed29 explicitly calls its Greek comparison slightly emended.
Printed30 proposes punctuation after מהם and deletion of אשר before נשבע; treats δύο as corruption connected with שנה. Its forty-year synopsis is not unmodified selected Greek.
Printed74 links21:42d with24:30a through literary reasoning and a proposed deletion motive; not independent manuscript proof.
Printed80's Hebrew continuation is expressly a possible rendering into Hebrew, not surviving manuscript text.
Ease of retroversion, fragmentary character, book division and ark-movement motives do not independently establish source priority.
Printed8–9 rejects the Shiloh alternatives despite the study's general preference for Greek; not blanket approval of Greek readings.
